A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProMoE work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, with retained material identifiable across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, routing ablations, scaling results, and token analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original text-to-image, expert-utilization, computational-cost, and clustering-comparison results.

M1.justification: The two-step router, contrastive loss, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix A adds an MM-DiT-style text-to-image instantiation with joint text/visual self-attention and visual-FFN experts. This variant uses four routed experts and one unconditional expert, without shared experts (Table 6), constituting a limited architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditional ImageNet generation. v2 additionally trains on a LAION-5B subset and evaluates text-to-image generation using GenEval, covering object composition, counting, colors, and spatial relations. Figure 14 adds corresponding prompted samples.

E2.justification: v2 adds GMM-based routing comparisons under top-1 and top-3 activation (Table 15). It also adds DiffMoE to the extended-training comparison previously containing dense DiT and ProMoE (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 12). Existing ImageNet comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new text-to-image protocol introduces 3B activated parameters, 400K training steps, GenEval evaluation, and 50-step UniPC sampling at CFG=5.0. Additional protocols include quantitative 2M-step comparisons at CFG=4.0, controlled timing measurements, utilization analysis on two 200-class subsets, and FID10K evaluation for the k-means sweep. Existing ImageNet settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 adds class-dependent expert-utilization analysis (Figure 6), k-means expert-count sensitivity (Appendix D.3), and measured computational-efficiency analysis (Appendix C.7). GMM comparisons under two activation settings additionally test an alternative to the proposed semantic routing (Appendix C.8).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new averaged utilization measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain unchanged, including the 2M-step rows moved from v1 Table 10 to v2 Table 12. Substantial new results include GenEval overall scores of 0.463 for ProMoE, 0.417 for Token-Choice MoE, and 0.390 for the dense model, plus additional extended-training, GMM, k-means sensitivity, utilization, and timing results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) and their mathematical definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised.

C1.justification: The scientific claims in the abstract, four contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same routing, specialization, performance, and scalability contributions. The added experiments expand supporting evidence without redefining those central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking measured costs to methodological efficiency and utilization/GMM results to specialization, while retaining the central redundancy-and-routing explanation. It also removes v1's explicit image-only validation and future multimodality limitation, retaining the FID/IS limitations paragraph.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds substantial text-to-image implementation information, including architecture, encoders, data subset, optimizer settings, hardware, and sampling, plus timing-measurement conditions. The abstract replaces promised future code with a stated availability link. However, the reproducibility statement remains outdated, still describing ImageNet-only experiments and future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GenEval, LAION-5B, Qwen2.5-VL, UniPC, and newer diffusion/tokenization work, and updates the diffusion-related-work paragraph. Its central positioning of explicit semantic guidance against existing implicit MoE routing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes terminology from 'standard experts' to 'routed experts,' clarifies selected paragraphs and appendix headings, and adds publication, contact, and acknowledgment text. The existing exposition and overall section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds several substantive tables, expert-utilization panels, and a prompted text-to-image sample grid. Table 5 gains a GFLOPs column, and v1 Table 10 is reorganized into v2 Tables 11–12 with expanded comparison columns and rows. Existing figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The LAION/GenEval experiment substantially addresses v1's ImageNet-only validation, while new utilization, clustering, extended-training, and timing analyses strengthen evidence about specialization and practical tradeoffs. Expanded implementation details also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the stale reproducibility statement and overbroad efficiency interpretation: Table 14 shows ProMoE remains slower at inference and requires roughly twice the training GPU-hours of dense DiT.
